cognate: *médhu 'mead' (Ved. mádhu, Gk μέθυ, OE medu, ON mjöðr) qualified by *swéh2du- 'sweet' (Ved. svādú/svā́diṣṭha/svā́dman, Gk ἡδύς, OE swēte): adjective + noun with both members cognate in three branches.
drift_or_renewal: Semantic drift of the noun: Gk μέθυ = (sweet) wine, Ved. mádhu = honey/sweet soma-drink, Gmc = mead (the old fermented honey drink). In Vedic the adjective is often in derived/superlative form (svā́diṣṭham mádhvaḥ, svā́dman … mádhūni). In ON the accompanying verb 'drink' is renewed (drekka for *peh3-, cf. Ved. píbati, Gk πίνω), giving 'drink mead' rather than 'sweet mead'.
shared_syntax: Attributive adjective + noun (μέθυ ἡδύ, swētne medo, svādv … madhu); Vedic also partitive-genitive object of 'drink' (mádhvaḥ … piba), as Gk μέθυ πίνετο.
context: Feast / drink-offering contexts in all three: Homeric feasting formula 'meat without end and sweet wine' (κρέα τ' ἄσπετα καὶ μέθυ ἡδύ), a lord's hospitality (σῖτον καὶ μέθυ ἡδύ given as provisions); Finnsburh 39 retainers 'repaying the sweet mead' given by their lord in the hall; Vedic invitation to the god to drink the sweetest mead at the offering. In all, the drink is the gift of the host and the warrior/guest's reward.
phrase: *swéh2dus médhu 'sweet mead' (pie-lex-sweh2dus + pie-lex-medhu), with *peh3- 'drink' as verb

cognate: *h1ed- 'eat' (Ved. ad-, Gk ἔδω, ON eta) with *krewh2- 'raw flesh/gore' (Ved. kravís, Gk κρέας, ON hrár 'raw'); Ved. āmá- 'raw' = Gk ὠμός (support: Il. 22.347 ὤμ' … κρέα ἔδμεναι, an exact *h2eh3mo- + *krewh2s + *h1ed- match to āmaṃ … kraviḥ adanti).
drift_or_renewal: ON hrár keeps the root as the adjective 'raw' while the noun is renewed (kjöt 'meat'); Gk κρέας generalised from 'raw flesh' to any meat, so rawness is expressed by ὠμός or implied (Cyclops). 'Human' is renewed per branch (Ved. pauruṣeya- from púruṣa-, Gk ἀνδρόμεος from ἀνήρ) but the notion 'human flesh' is shared by the AV and Od. 9 passages.
shared_syntax: Transitive 'eat' with the flesh (qualified as raw/human) as direct object: āmaṃ māṃsam … kraviḥ adanti ~ ἀνδρόμεα κρέ' ἔδων ~ kjöt hrátt eta.
context: Raw-flesh eating as the mark of the monstrous/uncivilised: AV 8.6 is a charm against flesh-eating demons who eat raw and human flesh; Od. 9 the man-eating Cyclops; Helgakviða Hundingsbana II (Völsungakviða forna) taunts warriors/vikings 'eating raw meat under helmets'; Il. 22.347 Achilles' wish to eat Hector raw is the extreme of savagery. The topos is the same negative frame, not neutral cooking language.
phrase: *h2eh3mom krewh2s h1ed- 'eat raw flesh' (pie-lex-h2eh3mos + pie-lex-krewh2s + pie-root-h1ed-eat)

cognate: *h1ed- 'eat' (Ved. ad-, Gk ἔδω/ἐσθίω, Lat. edo) coordinated with *peh3- 'drink' (Ved. píbati, Gk πίνω, Lat. bibo — Lat. bibō and Ved. píbati continue the same reduplicated present *pí-ph3-e-).
drift_or_renewal: Greek sometimes renews 'eat' by suppletive φαγεῖν (Simonides) and AV by aś- 'eat'; Germanic renews 'drink' (ON drekka) while keeping eta. The pairing itself is stable.
shared_syntax: Coordinated pair of verbs, eat + drink, often imperatives (Ved. addhi … pibā; Gk ἐσθίετε … πίνετε) or parallel finite verbs with optional objects (σῖτον ἔδουσ' … οἶνον; adát píbat).
context: Sustenance and hospitality / ritual feeding: Vedic invitations to a god or cow to eat and drink; Circe's invitation (Od. 10.460), Eumaeus feeding the guest (Od. 14.109); the gods who 'do not eat bread or drink wine' (Il. 5.341); Cato's dietary instruction. The merism 'eat and drink' = full nourishment. Genericness is a real risk (any language says this); the weight lies in exact cognate verbs in a fixed pair across three branches, and Hittite ed- / eku- 'eat and drink' as a frequent ritual pair (recalled, not in corpora checked).

cognate: *terp- 'be sated, take one's fill (of food/drink)' (Ved. tr̥p-, tr̥ptí-; Gk τέρπομαι) coordinated with *peh3- 'drink' (Ved. pītí-, píba; Gk πίνω).
drift_or_renewal: Gk τέρπομαι has broadened to 'enjoy oneself, delight' (Od. 15.391 'enjoy yourself and drink wine'; Hesiod's golden race 'delighting in feasts'), but keeps the old 'have one's fill of food and drink' in the Homeric formula τάρπημεν ἐδητύος ἠδὲ ποτῆτος; Vedic keeps 'be satisfied (with soma)'. Noun of drink renewed: Ved. soma/pītí vs Gk οἶνος/ποτής.
shared_syntax: 'Drink' + 'be sated' in coordination (pītím tr̥ptím 'drinking and satiety'; τέρπεο πῖνέ τε); in support both languages construe *terp- with a partitive genitive of what one is sated with (sómasya tr̥pṇuhi ~ τάρπησαν ἐδητύος ἠδὲ ποτῆτος).
context: Feast/drink-offering: Indra invited to obtain drink and satiety from the soma; Eumaeus bids the guest enjoy himself and drink wine; Hesiod's golden race delighting in feasts. Same host-to-guest (or worshipper-to-god) satisfaction frame.
phrase: *terp- (+gen. of food/drink) with *peh3- 'drink one's fill' (pie-root-terp-satisfy + pie-root-peh3-drink)

cognate: *yewg- 'yoke' (Ved. yuj-, Gk ζεύγνυμι/ζυγόν, Lat. iungo — Lat. iungō and Ved. yunákti/yuñjanti share the nasal present *yu-n-eg-) with *h1éḱwos 'horse' as object (Ved. áśva-, Gk ἵππος, Lat. equus).
drift_or_renewal: Greek prefers the periphrasis ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἄγειν ἵππους (with the cognate noun ζυγόν = Ved. yugá-, Lat. iugum) beside the verb ζεύγνυμι ἵππους (support); Vedic often names the team by colour words (hárī, harítaḥ) instead of áśva-. Od. 6.73 has mules for horses.
shared_syntax: Transitive 'yoke' with the horses as direct object, often with the chariot in the locative/dative ('to the chariot': ráthe; ὑφ' ἅρμασιν) or the purpose 'to drive' (yā́tave).
context: Harnessing for a chariot journey in all three; in particular the luminary's team: the Sun (Sūrya) yokes his mares to go (AVŚ 13.2.15, RV 9.63.9b) exactly as Lucretius' Sol re-yokes the scattered horses after Phaethon's fall (equos iunxit); Greek support Od. 23.244-6 Athena keeps Dawn from yoking her horses that bring light to men, matching RV 1.92.15 Dawn bidden to yoke her ruddy horses.
phrase: *h1éḱwons yewg- (pie-root-yewg-join + pie-lex-h1ekjwos), notably of the Sun's/Dawn's team

cognate: *h1óḱus 'swift' (Ved. āśú-, Gk ὠκύς) as epithet of the yoked team; with *h1éḱwos in support (Ved. āśúm áśvam ~ Gk ὠκέας ἵππους; Av. āsu.aspa-, recalled).
drift_or_renewal: In the anchor RV 1.118.4b the noun is renewed: the Aśvins' team is 'swift flyers' (āśávaḥ pataṃgā́ḥ, birds serving as horses), but they are 'yoked to the chariot' exactly as ὑπὸ ζυγὸν … ὠκέας ἵππους.
shared_syntax: Epithet + noun as object/subject of yoking: ráthe yuktā́saḥ āśávaḥ ~ ὕπαγε ζυγὸν ὠκέας ἵππους.
context: Harnessing the chariot team for a journey (Aśvins' chariot; Automedon and Menelaus yoking horses for battle/race). A known inherited formula (Schmitt) actually present in the packet.

cognate: The packet line h.Cer. 375 itself gives only ἵππους + ὄχεσφιν; 'immortal' (ἀθανάτους) stands in the adjacent context line 376, and the exact cognate ἄμβροτοι ἵπποι is only in support (Il. 16.381). Equation: *h1éḱwos (aśva ~ ἵππος) with 'immortal': Ved. amṛ́ta- = Gk ἄμβροτος < *n̥-mr̥tó- (support Il. 16.381 ἵπποι ἄμβροτοι); plus *weǵh- in the chariot (Ved. vahanti ratham; Gk ὄχεσφιν, ὄχος < *wóǵhos).
drift_or_renewal: In the packet anchor Greek uses ἀθάνατος (the productive replacement of ἄμβροτος in the same sense) in the next line (376); the exact cognate ἄμβροτοι ἵπποι survives in Iliad 16. Vedic 'chariot' is rátha- where Greek uses ὄχος (cognate with Ved. vah-/vā́ha-): the convey-root is kept in the noun in Greek and the verb in Vedic.
shared_syntax: Adjective 'immortal' agreeing with the horses who draw a (golden) chariot.
context: Divine teams: the Sun's immortal bay horses who always draw his chariot (AVŚ 13.1.47) vs the immortal horses yoked under the golden chariot of Hades (h.Cer. 375-6) and Achilles' god-given immortal horses (Il. 16).
phrase: *n̥mr̥tóes h1éḱwōs 'immortal horses' (pie-lex-nmrtos + pie-lex-h1ekjwos) drawing the god's chariot (*weǵh-)

cognate: *weǵh- 'convey (by vehicle)' with *h1éḱwos: Ved. áśvāḥ vahanti; Gk ἵπποισιν ὀχεῖσθαι (ὀχέω = Ved. vāhayati-type iterative *woǵh-éye-) and ἵπποισιν καὶ ὄχεσφιν (ὄχος < *wóǵhos 'vehicle').
drift_or_renewal: Diathesis shift: in Vedic the horses are subject of active vah- (they convey the god/chariot), in Greek the rider is subject of middle ὀχεῖται 'is conveyed' with horses in the instrumental dative; Greek also nominalises the root (ὄχεα 'chariot'), Vedic keeps rátha-.
shared_syntax: Horses as the agent/instrument of *weǵh- (nominative subject in Vedic; instrumental-dative ἵπποισι in Greek).
context: Travel of a god or hero by horse-team: Bhaga/Dawn brought by horses 'like a chariot' (RV 7.41.6, AVŚ 3.16.12), Dawn brought by her horses (RV 3.61.2); Anchises driven by storm-footed horses, warriors going 'with horses and chariot'. Low: the root is the ordinary verb of vehicular transport, so co-occurrence with 'horse' is expected.

cognate: A feminine *dyew-derivative as standing epithet of the Dawn/Sky's-daughter figure: Ved. devī́ (< *deywih2) uṣā́s; Gk δῖα (< *diwyh2) — in Homer Ἠὼς δῖα (support, 10x) and δῖα γυναικῶν of Helen (anchor), who is Διὸς θυγάτηρ as Uṣas is diváḥ duhitā́ (anchor RV 1.92.5d).
drift_or_renewal: Not the same derivative: devī́ is the feminine of devá- (*deywo-), δῖα the feminine of δῖος (*diwyo-, = Ved. divyá-); both 'belonging to the sky/divine' and built on *dyew-. In the packet's Greek anchor the noun is Helen, not Eos; the transfer rests on the (recalled, contested) identification of Helen with the Indo-European Sun-/Dawn-maiden, daughter of the Sky-god.
shared_syntax: Epithet + name (noun) in agreement, epithet adjacent to the name.
context: Dawn as the shining goddess, daughter of Dyaus (RV 1.92.5d, 3.61.5a) vs Homeric Ἠὼς δῖα and Helen δῖα γυναικῶν, daughter of Zeus. Congruence on the Greek side is supported only by the search witnesses (Eos) and by literature (Helen ~ Dawn/Sun-maiden), not by the packet passage itself.
